about: Chapter 1 narrative text pack for the Expedition Journal (Now, Evidence, Garden, Decisions, People and Science tabs), Growth Record caption templates, resume card templates, the EX-CH01-S03 drawer-lid note, the Chapter 1 mistake feedback sentence and the Alo Lost blame-free debrief text.
consumer_rules: Show an entry only after its trigger fires in the saved snapshot; nothing appears early.
Show a link only when the linked entry is already shown; links never preview later entries.
Gate titles and bodies by gate_flag, never by keyword (doc 24 section 6.5). Chapter 1 needs no gate flags: N. stays N.
surface 'journal' entries belong to the tabs; the other surfaces are the P-02 preview, the chapter debrief, the resume card and the Growth Record templates.
Fill {placeholders} only from the snapshot; a placeholders map lists the allowed words for a slot.
evidence_label uses the catalog domain: Simulated, Fiction or Computed-pending.

drawer_lid_note.inscription: Seed 1: outer chamber. Seed 2: inside, for comparison. Water at

entries.title: Sunlight routing traced
entries.body: The battery is full at 20 units while the solar mast keeps making power. Extra energy can fill the air tank or warm the planting bay instead of spilling.

entries.title: Commissioning route checked
entries.body: We compared storing extra air against lighting the planting bench. Both choices are safe and leave the April 25 night baseline unchanged.

entries.title: Station charter and stop rule
entries.body: Rafi turned the emergency card toward every seat at the table. Any cadet may stop the work when something seems unsafe.

entries.title: Local, stored and live-link paths
entries.body: Station sensors, suit radios and printed safety cards stay here at Aurora. Losing the live Earth screen only pauses long-distance conversation.

entries.title: Four crew name tokens
entries.body: Rafi placed four crew name tokens on the Safe Room board. Names stand for people, and we never trade a person for a resource.

entries.title: Practice fault cleared locally
entries.body: We solved the disconnected practice fault using the stored station card alone. The garden bench can be made safe before the crew steps into the shelter.

entries.title: Seed packet
entries.body: Two dry seeds, the word ALO and the initial N. The original stays sealed; we copied the label.

entries.title: Drawer lid
entries.body: A pencilled plan for two seeds: one outside, one inside for comparison. The last line stops at "Water at".

entries.title: Probe dry zero set
entries.body: The dry reference read 10 when it should read 0, so the probe was off by 10. Setting zero first keeps our soil readings honest.

entries.title: Probe wet span set
entries.body: We matched the moisture probe to the wet reference sample at 100. Now the scale between bone-dry and fully wet is fixed.

entries.title: Probe calibration verified
entries.body: Rechecking both reference blocks confirmed 0 dry and 100 wet with no drift. The probe is ready to measure the 40 to 60 planting moisture band.

entries.title: Two sealed plant chambers
entries.body: Both the outer test chamber and the indoor bay hold warm, pressurised air. Neither seed ever touches lunar vacuum.

entries.title: Planned two-chamber test
entries.body: Whoever left the seeds planned the same two-chamber test we are running. Something interrupted the note before the watering line was finished.

entries.title: Alo planted in outer chamber
entries.body: Mei guided the first seed into the sealed outer test cassette through the glove ports. Kai held the work light steady while the transfer lid stayed latched.

entries.title: Tara planted in reference bay
entries.body: The second seed from the same packet was planted in the indoor reference bay and named Tara. A reference plant gets the same careful care as the outer test plant.

entries.title: Alo watered to calibrated band
entries.body: We watered Alo's cassette to inside the 40 to 60 band. The calibrated probe checked the reading before we sealed it.

entries.title: Tara watered to calibrated band
entries.body: Tara's indoor cassette was watered to the same calibrated 40 to 60 moisture band. Matching starting water lets us compare the two chambers fairly.

entries.title: Alo labelled EXTERNAL TEST
entries.body: Alo's holder carries the label EXTERNAL TEST with today's planting date and seed lot. Clear labels keep our observations tied to the right chamber.

entries.title: Tara labelled INDOOR REFERENCE
entries.body: Tara's holder carries the label INDOOR REFERENCE beside her own close-up camera view. Both plants now have named places in the notebook.

entries.title: Alo cassette sealed
entries.body: The outer test cassette seal locked cleanly and held pressure. Alo is safe inside her pressurised enclosure.

entries.title: Tara cassette sealed
entries.body: Tara's indoor reference cassette seal closed and passed its check. Both seeds are now enclosed with warm air, water and light.

entries.title: Paired Growth Record started
entries.body: We wrote down the warmth, water and light beside the first photo of each plant. With the conditions next to each photo, later changes are easier to explain.

entries.title: Both chamber services confirmed
entries.body: Power, air, heat and water lines were verified for both plant chambers. The original seed packet is back in dry storage.

entries.title: Backup hand light hung ready
entries.body: Rafi hung a tested backup hand light handle-out beside the corridor locker. Its home is marked on the equipment board so anyone can reach it in the dark.

entries.title: Fourteen dated care entries
entries.body: We made fourteen dated care entries for both plants: moisture, connections, root photos and new leaves. Both Alo and Tara formed green buds on 18 April.

entries.title: Dated care complete
entries.body: The date card moved to 24 April only after every care visit was recorded. Both plants are in bud before the night plan begins on 25 April.

entries.title: Three separate night tracks
entries.body: Sunlight, the Earth radio link and station switches sit on separate timeline tracks. Two daylight shifts come before five dark shifts in this 36-hour training scenario.

entries.title: Shared night schedule checked
entries.body: With the shelter's water and the garden's watering on one board, we spotted a clash early. We added a time to send the water back before using anything.

entries.title: Four specialist crew notes
entries.body: Power, air, garden and safety cards each show part of the night budget. No single card can solve the seven shifts without the others.

entries.title: Daylight shift 1 locked in
entries.body: We locked in daylight shift 1 with the battery cap and the whole night in view. Kai wrote the reason beside the setting for the next watch.

entries.title: Daylight shift 2 prepared for the drill
entries.body: Shift 2 is prepared in the forecast and paused until the Safe Room drill finishes. Preparing it lets us check the whole night before we lock the second shift.

entries.title: Safe Room drill and roll call
entries.body: All four cadets counted themselves into the Safe Room and practised moving garden water into the shelter wall. The storm trace is a labelled replay of a real 2017 event.

entries.title: Pre-drill baseline unchanged
entries.body: Amara read the post-drill meters aloud to prove practice spent no real energy, air or water. Kai drew a return ticket arrow so we remember to send borrowed water back.

entries.title: Daylight shift 2 locked in at 18:00
entries.body: With the shelter drill complete, we locked in the second daylight shift at the 18:00 gate. The solar masts now approach sunset with reserves stored.

entries.title: Cold, thirst and storm cards combined
entries.body: Mei's card says cold and thirst are Alo's biggest dangers tonight, and Rafi's storm warning needs the same water for the shelter wall. Reading the two cards together lets us plan for the crew and the garden at once.

entries.title: Earth-link cutoff noted
entries.body: We read back Ferreira's last instruction before the Earth-link cutoff greyed out the live channel. Local rules and stored guidance stay active at Aurora.

entries.title: Dark shifts 3 and 4 resolved
entries.body: We locked in the first two dark shifts using stored power and local rules. The hand light stayed in its marked place.

entries.title: All four cadets sheltered
entries.body: When the instrument alarm rose in dark shift 5, Rafi called four names and waited for four answers. Every cadet was inside the Safe Room before we locked in a response.

entries.title: Shift 5 storm response locked in
entries.body: Mei asked Kai to read our chosen action back, so we acted as one team instead of rushing. One allowed response ran under the rules we practised.

entries.title: Exposure step verified complete
entries.body: Amara checked the instrument log to confirm the storm exposure step finished before touching the water valve. Shielding water stays in the wall until its job is done.

entries.title: Borrowed water returned to garden
entries.body: At a legal gate we drained the shelter wall back into the garden reservoir. The garden's water supply is open again.

entries.title: Final dark shifts 6 and 7 resolved
entries.body: We locked in the last two dark shifts, which end at 06:00 UTC on 27 April. The forecast checked every shift's demand against the stored energy.

entries.title: Night One causal outcome reviewed
entries.body: We reviewed the night shift by shift: what kept the crew safe and what happened to Alo's bud. The review names a cause, not a person.

entries.title: Outer chamber safe before shutter
entries.body: At dawn we checked the air pressure, warmth and water in Alo's outer chamber, and all were steady. We check safety before we celebrate.

entries.title: First bloom at dawn
entries.body: When we opened the viewing shutter, Alo had a yellow mustard flower with four petals. She came through the 36-hour night inside her sealed chamber.

entries.title: A recording, not a call
entries.body: It played when we tagged the bloom photo. Nobody could call us: the Earth link was down.

entries.title: Tara's bud in the reference bay
entries.body: Tara is still in bud in the indoor reference bay, on a healthy green stem. When the message said Alo needs a friend, Mei looked toward her.

entries.title: Night One debrief complete
entries.body: Our debrief separated the real 2017 storm record, the training schedule and the parts of Aurora's story that are fiction. The bloom photo now sits beside the sealed packet marked N.

entries.title: Left for a future bloom
entries.body: The voice signed N. was recorded before we arrived and set to play for a bloom. Whoever N. is expected someone to be here to hear it.

entries.title: Who is N.?
entries.body: Someone left two seeds in a packet marked ALO and N. Who is N., and when were they here?

entries.title: Why only two seeds?
entries.body: The drawer held only two seeds and a pencilled plan that stops in the middle of a line. Why two seeds, and why did the note stop?

entries.title: Why the name Alo?
entries.body: The packet is marked ALO, which means light. Why did the person who left the seeds choose that name?

entries.title: Why does Alo need a friend?
entries.body: The stored message says Alo needs a friend now that she has bloomed. What kind of friend does a flowering plant need, and could it be Tara?

entries.title: A full store can't take more
entries.body: Extra sunlight spills if the battery is already full. Check where energy can be used or stored before calling it spare.

learning.observe: Trying the plan first tells useful routing apart from overflow.
learning.explain: Available production is not unlimited storage.
learning.transfer: Check where energy can be used or stored before treating it as spare.

entries.title: Local rules work without Earth
entries.body: Losing the Earth radio link stops live calls, not the station's air, sensors or safety cards. A good emergency plan never depends on one phone line.

learning.predict: Which instructions disappear with a radio path?
learning.observe: Local cards, sensors and suit links remain.
learning.explain: Communications and life support are separate systems.
learning.transfer: A school emergency plan should not depend on one phone.

entries.title: Measurements need a reference
entries.body: A sensor number only makes sense after we check it against known dry and wet samples. Always check how an instrument was zeroed before trusting it.

learning.explain: A reading needs an instrument and a reference.
learning.transfer: Check how an instrument was zeroed before relying on it.

entries.title: Comparisons keep their conditions
entries.body: A plant photo means more when we write down the date, temperature, water and light beside it. Keeping both records together shows what really caused a change.

learning.observe: Dates and environment records accompany each image.
learning.explain: Outcomes need context to be interpreted.
learning.transfer: Record light and watering in a classroom growing comparison.

entries.title: Growth takes time and daily care
entries.body: Plants do not jump from seed to bud in one second; they grow through days of steady water, warmth and light. Keeping notes on ordinary days shows how the bud was earned.

learning.concept: Growth takes time and sustained care.
learning.predict: What happens between seed and bud?
learning.observe: Dated maintenance is retained in the montage.
learning.explain: Time compression need not imply instant biology.
learning.transfer: Keep records of ordinary days in a growing experiment.

entries.title: Separate tracks, linked schedules
entries.body: Sunlight, the Earth radio link and station switches change at different gates. Putting them on one timeline shows where shelter water and garden care overlap.

learning.observe: The tracks change at separate gates.
learning.explain: Timelines expose dependencies without conflating events.
learning.transfer: Separate deadlines, communications and resources in a project plan.

entries.title: One shared budget connects all roles
entries.body: Air makers, heaters and plant lamps all spend from the same stored power. Compare complete shift plans instead of looking at one system alone.

learning.concept: A shared resource budget connects systems.
learning.predict: Can one load change without affecting the forecast?
learning.observe: Every setting uses the same shared budget.
learning.explain: Compare whole plans rather than separate best cases.
learning.transfer: Agree on a single shared budget before promising separate outcomes.

entries.title: Borrowing water includes returning it
entries.body: The same water cannot fill the shelter wall and water the garden at the same time. Plan when shared equipment comes back before you borrow it.

learning.concept: Conservation and sequence in protective systems.
learning.predict: Can the same water be in both places?
learning.observe: The diagram moves a conserved reservoir.
learning.explain: Protection has secondary costs that need restoration.
learning.transfer: Plan the return of shared equipment before borrowing it.

entries.title: Different roles see the whole problem
entries.body: Storm protection and plant thirst use the same water tank. Combining Mei's and Rafi's observations lets us build a plan that works for both.

learning.concept: Information from different roles changes decisions.
learning.predict: Which two facts affect the water plan?
learning.observe: Storm risk and plant thirst share a reservoir.
learning.transfer: Ask what another person knows before locking in a shared plan.

entries.title: Prepared drills beat frantic clicks
entries.body: Clicking faster cannot collect two exclusive emergency actions at once. Following the agreed roll call and reading back one choice keeps the team safe.

learning.predict: Does more frantic input always help?
learning.explain: Resources and procedure determine a safe response.
learning.transfer: Follow an agreed drill sequence rather than inventing simultaneous tasks.

entries.title: Recovery completes a safety plan
entries.body: Wait until the storm exposure finishes before draining the shelter wall, then send the water home to the garden. Emergency actions need a clear end step.

learning.predict: When can a protective resource return?
learning.observe: Exposure, drainage and later plant effects occur in order.
learning.transfer: Check safe restoration after using emergency supplies.

entries.title: Stored media versus live contact
entries.body: The bloom message played because tagging the flower photo started a file stored at Aurora. Checking where a message comes from tells a recording apart from a live call.

learning.concept: Evidence distinguishes stored media from live contact.
learning.predict: Why does a message play while Earth is unavailable?
learning.observe: The recorder shows its local origin and event trigger.
learning.explain: A stored message can respond to a local event.
learning.transfer: Distinguish recorded messages from live conversations.

entries.title: Sunlight We Cannot Keep
entries.body: Trace where the spare sunlight goes, choose stored air or the planting bay, and read the station charter. This is the crew's first decision at Aurora.
entries.objective_text: Trace where the spare sunlight goes, choose stored air or the planting bay, and read the station charter.
entries.completed_text: You routed spare commissioning sunlight and accepted Aurora's safety charter.

entries.title: The Rule That Works Without Earth
entries.body: Sort local, stored and Earth-link information, run the four-person roll call, and clear the practice fault. A safe station has to work even when Earth cannot answer.
entries.objective_text: Sort local, stored and Earth-link information, run the four-person roll call, and clear the practice fault.
entries.completed_text: You completed the four-person roll call and solved the practice fault using local rules.

entries.title: A Label Older Than Our Names
entries.body: Calibrate the moisture probe, inspect the sealed seed packet, and compare both plant chambers. Two old seeds need a fair beginning.
entries.objective_text: Calibrate the moisture probe, inspect the sealed seed packet, and compare both plant chambers.
entries.completed_text: You calibrated the moisture probe and inspected the sealed ALO seed packet.

entries.title: Two Places for a Beginning
entries.body: Plant, water, label and seal one seed in each cassette, then record their conditions. Each plant gets its own place and its own record.
entries.objective_text: Plant, water, label and seal one seed in each cassette, then record their conditions.
entries.completed_text: You planted Alo outside and Tara inside and opened their paired Growth Record.

entries.title: An Important Scientific Lamp
entries.body: Hang the backup hand light, then complete the dated care visits for both plants. Time moves on only after each day's care is recorded.
entries.objective_text: Hang the backup hand light, then complete the dated care visits for both plants.
entries.completed_text: You hung the backup hand light and logged fourteen care entries through first buds.

entries.title: The Night Has a Shape
entries.body: Put the Sun, Earth-link and station tracks in order, then check the shared night schedule. A long night is easier to face when it has a timetable.
entries.objective_text: Put the Sun, Earth-link and station tracks in order, then check the shared night schedule.
entries.completed_text: You aligned the three night timeline tracks and scheduled the water return.

entries.title: Air Before the Jar Spills
entries.body: Read the four crew notes, lock in daylight shift 1, and prepare shift 2 without locking it in. What the station stores in daylight has to last the dark shifts.
entries.objective_text: Read the four crew notes, lock in daylight shift 1, and prepare shift 2 without locking it in.
entries.completed_text: You combined the four crew notes, locked in daylight shift 1, and prepared shift 2.

entries.title: Borrowing Includes Returning
entries.body: Practise the shelter drill, check that practice cost nothing, and lock in daylight shift 2 at 18:00. Water the shelter borrows has to go back to the garden.
entries.objective_text: Practise the shelter drill, check that practice cost nothing, and lock in daylight shift 2 at 18:00.
entries.completed_text: You practised the shelter drill and locked in daylight shift 2.

entries.title: The Horizon Closes One Door
entries.body: Read Mei's cold-and-thirst card with Rafi's warning, note the Earth-link cutoff, then resolve dark shifts 3 and 4. From here the crew works with local rules and stored guidance.
entries.objective_text: Read Mei's cold-and-thirst card with Rafi's warning, note the Earth-link cutoff, then resolve dark shifts 3 and 4.
entries.completed_text: You noted the Earth-link cutoff and resolved dark shifts 3 and 4.

entries.title: The Choice Inside the Rules
entries.body: Confirm all four cadets are in the Safe Room, then choose one WAIT, PUMP or STACK response. The crew goes inside first, every time.
entries.objective_text: Confirm all four cadets are in the Safe Room, then choose one WAIT, PUMP or STACK response.
entries.completed_text: You sheltered all four cadets and resolved the shift 5 storm alarm.

entries.title: Send the Water Home
entries.body: Check that the exposure has resolved, return the borrowed water, and resolve dark shifts 6 and 7. The water goes home only after it has finished protecting the crew.
entries.objective_text: Check that the exposure has resolved, return the borrowed water, and resolve dark shifts 6 and 7.
entries.completed_text: You returned the borrowed water after the exposure resolved and completed shifts 6 and 7.

entries.title: Alo Needs a Friend
entries.body: Check the chamber, open the viewing shutter and record what you see, then look in on Tara. Safety checks come before celebrating.
entries.objective_text: Check the chamber, open the viewing shutter and record what you see, then look in on Tara.
entries.completed_text: You opened the shutter on Alo's first flower, heard N.'s stored message, and checked Tara's bud.

entries.body: {plant_name} ({chamber_label}) on {date}: growth {stage_label}, moisture {moisture}, heat {heat_label}, light {light_label}.

entries.title: Life-cycle track caption
entries.body: Life cycle from seed to sprout, bud, flower, pods and ripe seeds. {plant_name} is now in the {stage_label} phase.

entries.title: Alo, 11 April
entries.body: Planted in the sealed outer test chamber, labelled EXTERNAL TEST. Moisture set inside the calibrated 40 to 60 band.

entries.title: Tara, 11 April
entries.body: Planted in the indoor reference bay, labelled INDOOR REFERENCE. Same seed packet, same 40 to 60 moisture band.

entries.title: Alo, 12 April
entries.body: Two seed leaves open. Moisture inside the calibrated band.

entries.title: Tara, 12 April
entries.body: Two green seed leaves open in the indoor reference bay. Moisture and warmth stay steady beside Alo's record.

entries.title: Alo, 18 April
entries.body: Rough-edged true leaves and a tight green bud cluster at the stem tip.

entries.title: Tara, 18 April
entries.body: True leaves open and a tight green bud cluster forms in the indoor reference bay.

entries.title: Alo, 27 April
entries.body: Four yellow petals open in a cross when the viewing shutter opens at dawn. First flower in the outer chamber.

entries.title: Tara, 27 April
entries.body: Still in bud, on a healthy green stem in the indoor reference bay. Her care went on through the whole night.

entries.usage: Only when the crew is split (doc 24 section 6.6, line 2). Chapter 1 never shows it.

entries.body: Now: {current_objective}

entries.body: Open question: {open_question}

entries.title: Spare sunlight → stored air
entries.body: We routed spare commissioning sunlight into the air tank. The air gauge rose in the exercise and a Day-one photo was saved.

entries.title: Spare sunlight → planting bay
entries.body: We routed spare commissioning sunlight to the planting bay lamp. The empty garden glowed until 25 April and a Day-one photo was saved.

entries.title: Notebook layout → paired photographs
entries.body: We set up the Growth Record as paired dated photographs for Alo and Tara. Side-by-side photos make changes in shape and size easy to spot.

entries.title: Notebook layout → paired conditions table
entries.body: We set up the Growth Record as a paired conditions table for Alo and Tara. Comparing temperature, moisture and light side by side explains why each plant changes.

entries.title: Rehearsal lead → Rafi
entries.body: Rafi led the local emergency rehearsal from his printed checklist. All four cadets confirmed the same shutdown and roll-call order.

entries.title: Rehearsal lead → Amara
entries.body: Amara read the local procedure back to test a second user on the card. All four cadets confirmed the same shutdown and roll-call order.

entries.title: First record → packet provenance
entries.body: We copied the ALO seed packet record first so seed handling was traceable from the start. Then we calibrated the moisture probe before planting.

entries.title: First record → calibration result
entries.body: We logged the moisture probe reference check first so every measurement had a clear zero and span. Then we copied the ALO seed packet label.

entries.title: Beside latest image → first photograph
entries.body: We placed the 12 April sprout photograph beside the 24 April bud image. With the first and latest photos together, two weeks of growth are easy to see.

entries.title: Beside latest image → conditions record
entries.body: We placed the fourteen-day care and conditions log beside the 24 April bud image. Showing the daily water and heat readings highlights the work behind the bud.

entries.title: Tested keeping water in wall all night
entries.body: We tested keeping borrowed water in the shelter wall for the whole night in the paused forecast. That trial showed how an unreturned loan leaves the garden thirsty.

entries.title: Tested returning water after exposure
entries.body: We tested sending the water back as soon as the storm exposure it shields had passed. The forecast showed less shielding later but water back for the garden, so we checked both.

entries.title: Daylight forecast → stored-air priority
entries.body: We tested making extra stored air first, inside the same daylight energy limit. The forecast showed that air making and the lamp share one battery.

entries.title: Daylight forecast → garden-lamp priority
entries.body: We tested putting the garden lamp first within the same daylight budget. The forecast showed the plant benefit and the air and energy the rest of the night still needed.

entries.title: Water return reminder → timeline marker
entries.body: We marked the water return on the shift timeline so the return gate stands out clearly. Everyone can see when the borrowed water goes back to the garden.

entries.title: Water return reminder → reservoir diagram
entries.body: We marked the water return on the shared reservoir flow diagram. Following the arrow shows that shelter shielding and garden water come from one tank.

entries.title: Dark plan comparison → shelter timeline first
entries.body: We started the dark-shift comparison from the shelter and water-return timeline. Checking protection first showed how much energy was left for heat and lamps.

entries.title: Dark plan comparison → heat-and-lamp timeline first
entries.body: We started the dark-shift comparison from the chamber heat and lamp timeline. Tracing plant needs first showed when the shelter water had to return.

entries.title: Shift 5 response → prepared WAIT
entries.body: With all four cadets inside, we confirmed WAIT because the forecast showed the prepared shelter was enough. No extra water or crates were created.

entries.title: Shift 5 response → PUMP or STACK intervention
entries.body: With all four cadets inside, we read back one PUMP or STACK action for shift 5 and locked it in. The forecast then showed what the rest of the night had left.

entries.title: Outcome review lead → water-return timeline
entries.body: We started the Night One review with the water-return timeline. It showed how sending the shelter water back on time gave Alo's garden its water again.

entries.title: Outcome review lead → demand-and-energy record
entries.body: We led the Night One review with the demand-and-energy log. It showed that a low battery at dawn is still safe when every shift demand is paid.

entries.title: Bloom caption → four role decisions
entries.body: We paired Alo's first-bloom photo with the four specialists' decisions across the night. The archive highlights how teamwork kept the flower alive.

entries.title: Bloom caption → care-and-recovery timeline
entries.body: We paired Alo's first-bloom photo with the full care and water-recovery timeline from 11 to 27 April. The archive highlights the steady daily work behind the bloom.

entries.title: Kai and the backup hand light
entries.body: Kai checked the corridor switch twice. Rafi hung a hand light beside the locker, handle out.

entries.title: Four named mugs
entries.body: After Alo's first flower opened, the four nameless mugs in the commons got the cadets' names. Aurora feels like their station now.

entries.title: Water drain blocked
entries.body: The wall is still shielding the next exposure. Drain after it resolves.

entries.title: Alo Lost debrief
entries.body: Alo did not survive the night in this attempt. Your checkpoint keeps her alive at the start of shift 5.
entries.body_template: Alo did not survive the night in this attempt. Your checkpoint keeps her alive at the start of shift {checkpoint_shift}.
entries.usage: body is the doc 24 section 2.10 sentence, true when Alo is alive at the start of shift 5. If her health reached 0 earlier, render body_template with the last shift that began with Alo alive.

entries.title: What we planned
entries.body: Here is the seven-shift plan we locked in: heat, air, light and water for every shift.

entries.title: What happened
entries.body: Alo's health fell from {start_health} to 0 by shift {loss_shift}. Each drop is marked on the shift where it happened.

entries.title: Why
entries.body: {cause_text}
entries.source: Mission Table shift record and its Data Card

cause_text.cold: The chamber heater ran on COOL or COLD in the dark, and each of those shifts cost Alo health. Saving power on heat was paid for by the plant.
cause_text.thirst: The shelter wall held 4 or more units of water, so the garden was short of water. Alo lost health in every shift the water stayed in the wall.
cause_text.dark: The garden light was OFF, and Alo lost a little health in each of those shifts. Plants need light to keep growing.
cause_text.blackout: One shift asked for more energy than the battery held, so the station blacked out. A blackout costs Alo 2 health at once.

entries.title: What we would change
entries.body: {change_question}

change_question.cold: Which dark shift could spend 1 more energy on heat?
change_question.thirst: When could the shelter water go back to the garden, once the exposure it shields has resolved?
change_question.dark: Which shift could afford DIM light instead of OFF?
change_question.blackout: Which setting could wait so that every shift's demand is paid?

entries.title: Try again from here
entries.body: Restore the checkpoint at the start of shift {checkpoint_shift}, {checkpoint_time}. All four cadets, Alo and every reading return to that moment.
